sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Erie County
sections.html:
Erie County deeds are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds, a division of the Erie County Clerk of Records. The office is in Room 121 of Erie County Courthouse I, 140 W. Sixth Street, Erie, PA 16501. Call 814-451-6246, fax 814-451-6213, or write to recorder@eriecountypa.gov.

The office reviews, records and indexes every document that touches Erie County real estate, then makes those records open to the public and to title professionals. Between 100 and 400 documents arrive each day. A deed with a missing page or the wrong fee can sit in a pile of returns, which delays the new owner's name appearing in the record.

The recorder also collects money for others: the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, the Department of State, and the municipalities and school districts in the county. The office is not funded by county tax dollars, and the county says it brings in more than it spends. Staff can't give legal advice about your deed. Send questions about wording to a lawyer or your title company.

The base fee for an Erie County deed is $87.00 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. Mortgages and a few other conveyance-type papers carry the same base fee, and smaller instruments cost less.

Erie County base recording fees, schedule effective December 1, 2025
InstrumentBase fee
Deed, mortgage, excerpt of adjudication, declaration of acquisition$87.00
Mortgage satisfaction, assignment or release$59.75
Easement, right of way, land contract$59.75
Lease over 30 years$59.75
Lease under 30 years, agreement exempt from transfer tax, all other instruments$18.50
UCC filing$100.00
Subdivision or land development map$30.00

Add-ons apply when a document runs larger than the base covers.

  • Indexed names over four: $0.50 each
  • Pages over four: $2.00 each
  • Additional parcels: $0.50 each
  • Statement of Value: $2.00
  • Copies picked up, emailed or faxed: $0.25 per page
  • Certification: $1.00 per document

Each amount carries an asterisk on the schedule. Ask the office to confirm the final total before anyone cuts a closing check.

sections.h2: Realty transfer tax on a home sale
sections.html:
Yes, Erie County charges it. The office collects Pennsylvania and local realty transfer tax on all realty transfers and passes the money to the Commonwealth and to the municipality or school district. The county points to 72 P.S. Section 8101-C and following, and 61 Pa. Code Section 91.101 and following, as the governing rules.

Some transfers are exempt. The county gives transactions between husband and wife, between parent and child, and between siblings as examples. Don't assume a family sale qualifies. The claim is made on the Statement of Value form, and the recorder reviews what the paper shows.

  • The Statement of Value costs $2.00 to record.
  • The Common Level Ratio changes with the fiscal year, so ask the recorder which factor applies to the date on your document.
  • The local rate depends on the municipality. Ask the office for the rate in your township, borough or city.

Buyer and seller divide the tax the way the sales agreement says. It scales with the sale price, so it is usually a bigger line on the settlement statement than the recording fee itself.

sections.h2: Searching Erie County deeds and ordering copies
sections.html:
The Recorder posts an online index and document images through Infocon, at www.infoconcountyaccess.com. Title companies and other filers can use the office's E-Recording information page.

A fire destroyed the Erie County Courthouse on March 23, 1823, and records made before that date were lost. Anyone tracing a very old chain of title should expect gaps and ask the office what survives.

To record by mail, send the package to Recorder of Deeds, 140 West 6th Street, Room 121, Erie, PA 16501. Enclose the right fees and a Statement of Value if one is needed. Put a return address on the package so the recorded deed finds its way back to you.

sections.h2: Checklist before you send a deed
sections.html:
Most of what slows a recording is avoidable. Before the closing package leaves your hands, run through this list.

  • Count the pages and the indexed names. Pages over four and names over four are billed extra.
  • List every parcel. Additional parcels are $0.50 each.
  • Attach the Statement of Value, and fill in any exemption claim on it.
  • Include one payment that covers the recording fee and the transfer tax. Call 814-451-6246 to confirm the total.
  • Add a return address.

If your title company handles the closing, ask whether it records electronically. That skips the mail and usually gets the deed into the index sooner. Once the deed is recorded, the new owner's name is public record, and the sale is complete as far as the county is concerned.

The deed is signed at the closing table, then the title company or attorney sends it to the recorder with the fees and the Statement of Value. Staff review it for the items listed above, charge the fees, and index it by name. Only then does the public record show the new owner.

If something is wrong, the office returns the package. A missing page, a wrong fee or an unsigned form means you start the clock again. If you are selling and want to know where your deed stands, call 814-451-6246 and ask. Keep a copy of everything you send, and keep the return address current so the recorded original reaches the right person.

Sellers who plan to hand over the house quickly should talk with the closing agent early about who is sending the deed and how. A package that is mailed, rather than sent electronically, takes longer to arrive and longer to come back.

sections.h2: Other fees on the Erie County schedule
sections.html:
A few items on the schedule come up around a sale. A notary appointment or renewal is $30.50 plus a $3.50 prothonotary fee. A storm water management map, planned community map or condominium plan is $30.00, the same as a subdivision map.

The county also collects low-income housing fees and record management fees along with Erie County recording fees and the Pennsylvania writ tax. State law or local ordinance sets every fee and tax, so the recorder can't negotiate them.

Erie County is the northernmost county in Pennsylvania, with Lake Erie along its northern edge. It has two cities, Erie and Corry, plus Millcreek, Harborcreek, Summit and Fairview townships and boroughs such as Edinboro, North East, Girard, Waterford and Union City.

The county has 265,832 residents in the July 2025 estimate, a 1.9% drop from the April 2020 base, and 120,762 housing units. The median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $177,000.

faqs.q: What is the base fee to record a deed in Erie County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $87.00 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. Pages over four are $2.00 each and indexed names over four are $0.50 each.

faqs.q: Where do I send a deed for recording in Erie County?
faqs.a: Mail it to Recorder of Deeds, 140 West 6th Street, Room 121, Erie, PA 16501. The office phone is 814-451-6246.

faqs.q: Are family transfers exempt from Erie County transfer tax?
faqs.a: Some are. The county names transfers between husband and wife, parent and child, and siblings as examples. You claim the exemption on the Statement of Value.

faqs.q: How much does a Statement of Value cost in Erie County?
faqs.a: It costs $2.00 on the current schedule. Additional parcels are $0.50 each.

faqs.q: Can I search Erie County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes. The office offers an online index and images through Infocon at www.infoconcountyaccess.com. Copies picked up or emailed are $0.25 per page.
